page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized, network-enhanced virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Hardware support includes AVX-512 vector extensions alongside standard cryptographic acceleration. It delivers 128.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive workloads.

The instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage and relies exclusively on remote Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes. It features a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps and lacks integrated GPU acceleration. In synthetic processing benchmarks, single-threaded metrics reflect conservative performance that registers within the lower tier of cloud CPUs, scoring 1,122.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1,283.59 in stress-ng. However, multithreaded scaling achieves balanced mid-tier results, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,004.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14,138.82.

Memory subsystem testing demonstrates dependable sustained bandwidth, recording 87.18 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB block reads and 48.4 GB/sec for large block writes. Cached small-block memory reads scale to 753.69 GB/sec. Application-oriented evaluations confirm stable throughput, delivering 13.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving rate of 11.9 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression operations remain lower tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 37.34 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure perspective, the r5n.4xlarge provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for architectures requiring significant RAM allocation without the premium of dedicated hardware accelerators. The balance between 16 vCPUs, 128 GB of RAM, and 16 Gbps networking makes it an appropriate platform for medium-scale in-memory key-value caches like Redis or Memcached, transactional database backends, search index engines, and enterprise ETL pipelines that do not depend on high single-core execution speed.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro instance designed for data-intensive and network-demanding applications. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores at 3.1 GHz) and 128 GB of DDR4 memory, it establishes an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is entirely decoupled, requiring external EBS volumes, while bundled network bandwidth reaches 16 Gbps without GPU hardware. Benchmark results display modest single-core CPU execution alongside balanced multithreaded and memory bandwidth performance, with uncached read throughput measuring 87.18 GB/sec and Redis key-value workloads exceeding 13 million operations per second. The instance provides cost-efficient memory density for in-memory caching, distributed database systems, search clusters, and batch data processing.
